summary: The original compiles and runs without error but emits a single constant colour — pure red (255,0,0) on EVERY pixel, under every rig, pixel count, seed, wall clock and time offset tested — so the pattern's defining feature (per-pixel random colours) never appears and no comparison with the port is obtainable; the score of 0 records 'no comparison obtainable', not port quality (the port's solo render looks like a sane static random-colour field).
observations: Both sides are STATIC fields: motion 0 and motionLit 0 on all 120 captured frames at 20 fps, zeroMotionFrames 120/120, brightnessTrend steady on both; --dump comparisons at t=0 vs t=0.5 s and at t=120 s vs t=125 s are byte-identical on both sides, so the temporal machinery (regimes, autocorrelation, fps coupling) is a no-op here and I pivoted to rig-geometry sweeps per JUDGE.md.

ORIGINAL (baseline, strip 60 px): every pixel is exactly [255,0,0]. statsSummary meanR 255 / meanG 0 / meanB 0, meanBrightness 85 constant. Unique colours in a frame: 1. Rendered as a waterfall it is a featureless solid red rectangle. No compileError and no runtimeError are reported.

The original's solid red is invariant to EVERYTHING the harness can vary: --pixels 12 / 30 / 60 / 300 / 600, --rig grid --grid 8x8, --rig cloud (5x5x5), --seed 1 / 7 / 1234 / 987654, --wall-clock 1756000000 vs 1700003333, and --skip 120 (2400 warm-up frames). origAllRed=true and origUniqueColours=1 in all 12 dumps. There is no warm-up transient and no late regime.

255,0,0 is exactly hsv(0, 1, 1), i.e. hue collapsed to 0 with full saturation and value — the signature of the pattern's random hue source returning a constant 0 in our engine rather than of a pattern that means to draw red.

Harness-sanity control (unrelated slug chill-confetti, labels srccheck-judge-src / seedchk-judge-src-a / seedchk-judge-src-b): its ORIGINAL renders varied, moving content (mean 13, motion 3) and its dumped frame hash CHANGES between --seed 1 (a397ad63bd39) and --seed 987654 (a1a233e7faf4). So the harness, the engine and the seeded RNG are all healthy, and --seed genuinely reaches the original engine — the failure is specific to this pattern (plausibly randomness consumed at init/top-level rather than inside render, but that is inference, not output evidence).

PORT (baseline, strip 60 px): a static field of per-pixel fully-saturated-ish colours — meanR 154 / meanG 152 / meanB 155, meanBrightness 154 constant. The waterfall is a set of vertical rainbow stripes, one colour per pixel, unchanging in time. This is what the slug name describes, so on its own the port looks correct.

Port colour statistics over 600 px (--pixels 600, HSV): value is exactly 1.0 on 600/600 pixels (every pixel has one channel at 255); hue is uniform over [0,1) (deciles 57,55,67,45,56,56,73,54,58,79); saturation spans 0.004..1.0 with avg 0.742 and a heavy mass in the top decile (276/600) over a mildly rising spread below it. So: uniform random hue, non-uniform saturation weighted toward saturated, constant full value.

The port's colour sequence is a FIXED sequence in pixel-index order: the first 6/12/60 pixel colours are byte-identical across strip 12 px, strip 60 px, strip 300 px and the 8x8 grid, and identical across seeds 1/7/1234/987654 and across wall clocks. Given that --seed demonstrably perturbs other patterns' port RNG (confetti control above), the port's field is not drawn from the harness-seeded RNG — it is a deterministic function of pixel index (or an internally re-seeded constant RNG), so it shows the same 'random' field on every run/boot.
Control surface: --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' on BOTH sides, and meta.json's controls list is empty for orig and port. No control-surface mismatch; dials are genuinely absent.
Neither side binds sensor globals (wantsSensors false on both), so the beat120 feed is irrelevant here.
feedback: This pair cannot be judged until the ORIGINAL renders something other than uniform red. The original's output is a single constant colour under every configuration I could vary, which is the exact hsv(0,1,1) point — the engine is producing hue 0 where the original expects random hues. Since the seeded RNG demonstrably works on other slugs' originals (chill-confetti's original changes with --seed), suspect randomness that is consumed OUTSIDE the per-frame render path (top-level/init code, or a per-pixel table filled once before rendering starts) rather than a dead random() builtin. Fix that engine gap, then re-run this slug before scoring the port.

Do NOT treat this verdict as evidence against the port. On its own the port produces exactly what the slug name implies: an unchanging per-pixel random-colour field, full value, uniform hue, mostly-saturated.

One port property worth checking once the original is comparable: the port's field is bit-identical across seeds 1/7/1234/987654 and across rig sizes, i.e. the same 'random' colours in the same pixel order every time. If the original re-randomizes per load (as a Pixel Blaze random() at init would), the port should consume the seeded RNG too rather than a fixed index-derived sequence; a viewer reloading the pattern would expect a different field, not the identical one.

Second port property to verify later: the port's saturation distribution is not uniform — avg 0.742 with ~46% of pixels in the top decile and a rising ramp below — while value is pinned at exactly 1.0 for every pixel. If the original turns out to draw hsv(random, 1, 1) (uniform hue, saturation exactly 1), the port is adding a saturation spread that should not be there; if the original spreads saturation, check the shape matches.
